report:
## Report: Do Face Masks Cause Dangerous CO2 Buildup?

**Conclusion:** The evidence does not support the claim that prolonged use of cloth or surgical face masks causes dangerous carbon dioxide buildup.

The World Health Organization (WHO) explicitly states that "the prolonged use of medical masks when properly worn, DOES NOT cause CO2 intoxication nor oxygen deficiency," acknowledging only that masks can be uncomfortable (https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters).

A peer-reviewed study published in the *Annals of the American Thoracic Society* by Samannan et al. examined gas exchange in both healthy individuals and patients with severe COPD—a group at higher risk for CO2 retention. The study found that neither cloth nor surgical masks impaired oxygenation or ventilation, even during physical activity (https://academic.oup.com/annalsats/article/18/3/541/8419544).

Multiple fact-checking organizations corroborate this. USA Today's fact check noted that while CO2 can accumulate slightly within a mask, the CDC considers it unlikely to cause hypercapnia (https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/05/30/fact-check-wearing-face-mask-not-cause-hypoxia-hypercapnia/5260106002/). Full Fact concluded that "wearing a mask is safe for most people," with rare exceptions involving tight-fitting respirators like N95s (https://fullfact.org/health/masks-not-harmful/).

Some fringe sources claim masks cause CO2 poisoning, but these are contradicted by the WHO, CDC, and peer-reviewed research. The consensus is clear: properly worn cloth and surgical masks do not cause dangerous carbon dioxide buildup.
